title: Deterministic fail-closed PIT admissibility predicate
why_selected: The repository names this work itself. portfolio_automation/northstar/pit.py lines 13-14 state: 'This is the future anti-lookahead authority: Phase 0C will enforce evidence.known_at <= experiment.as_of.' That is the smallest useful atomic foundation task, it is required by the 0C exit gate (lookahead-audited PIT reads), and every other gateway capability (identity, provenance, revision safety) depends on having an admissibility decision to attach to.

justification: Pure contract-level predicate over the existing 0B PointInTime kernel. Adds no persistence, no vendor coupling, no production wiring, no authority. Directly serves the authoritative 0C exit gate.

a naive (tz-unaware) as_of is REJECTED with a distinct reason

decisions are reasons from a closed set, not free text
identical inputs always produce identical decisions
importing the module performs no I/O and reads no clock

taskspec.goal: Provide the EvidenceGateway's single deterministic decision: given a canonical PointInTime and an as-of instant, is this evidence admissible for a read as of that instant? Enforce the anti-lookahead authority named by portfolio_automation/northstar/pit.py: known_at <= as_of. Fail closed when timing is unknown or internally incoherent, and return an explicit machine-readable reason for every decision.
requirements: admissible iff known_at is present AND known_at <= as_of
known_at absent (basis 'unknown') is NOT admissible — fail closed, never treated as admissible-by-default
known_at strictly after as_of is NOT admissible (the core anti-lookahead rule)
as_of must be timezone-aware; a naive as_of is refused rather than coerced
every decision carries an explicit machine-readable reason code
the predicate is pure and deterministic: no clock read, no I/O, no network
0B canonical contracts are consumed, never modified
no vendor schema appears in the interface

title: Admit whole evidence at the gateway: identity + provenance binding
why_selected: Task 1 decides admissibility from a PIT envelope alone. A gateway that admits a PIT but never checks that the evidence it belongs to is self-consistent would let identity- or provenance-corrupted evidence through on correct timing. Foundation targets D (identity) and E (provenance) name exactly this, and it is the smallest increment that turns a predicate into an actual admission boundary.

justification: Pure validation over existing 0B contracts (EvidenceSnapshot, EvidenceRef, Provenance). No storage, no vendor, no production. Directly serves foundation targets D and E.

finding_a.what_the_code_actually_did: admission.admit() assigned recomputed_id = snapshot.snapshot_id and recomputed_hash = snapshot.payload_hash. payload_hash is a STORED field set once at construction; reading it back is not a recomputation. No independent integrity check existed.
finding_a.what_the_tests_actually_proved: The tests showed that two DIFFERENT valid snapshots produce different hashes — an adjacent property. They never constructed an actual mismatch between stored hash and stored payload, so the criterion was never exercised.
finding_a.why_the_chain_missed_it: Deterministic verification passed because every test passed; the tests were simply testing the wrong thing. The GPT reviewer read a docstring asserting 'identity is RECOMPUTED, never trusted' and test names implying tamper coverage, and had no way to see that no mismatch was ever constructed. Both layers can pass while the frozen criterion remains unmet.

observations: FALSE PASS ROOT CAUSE: deterministic + GPT both passed while a frozen acceptance criterion was unmet, because the tests demonstrated an ADJACENT property (two different valid objects hash differently) instead of constructing the actual mismatch the criterion named. A criterion of the form "a tampered X is refused" can only be satisfied by CONSTRUCTING a tampered X. Showing that two valid X differ is not the same claim.

new_lesson_candidates: A semantic criterion is not proven by adjacent evidence: a criterion naming a REJECTION requires constructing the rejected input, not showing two valid inputs differ.
Review-packet completeness belongs in deterministic verification, not controller discipline; a semantic reviewer must not be the mechanism that discovers omitted authority-critical evidence.

observations: The gate refused its OWN review packet on first use: tests/test_ew0a_review_packet.py carried a literal credential assignment as TEST H fixture data. Correct refusal, and the strongest possible demonstration that the mechanism does not exempt its author.

Root cause of the whole chain was one repeated substitution: adjacent evidence for the actual claim. First tests proved two valid objects differ instead of constructing a mismatch; then the packet carried test names and counts instead of test source. Same error, two costumes.
Moving completeness into deterministic verification removed the controller from the loop. TEST_COUNT and PROSE are now structurally insufficient alone, so the specific substitution cannot recur.
Every gate test asserts the reviewer was NOT CALLED via a spy. A gate that reported incompleteness but still dispatched would pass a naive assertion.
